nodes.name: Electrospinning and Heat Treatment
nodes.procedure: The polyacrylonitrile (PAN) and Ru3+/Fe3+ metal salts were uniformly mixed in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF). Then the Ru-Fe7C3@CNF catalyst was obtained by electrospinning, pre-oxidation, and annealing steps. Detailed synthesis method is described in the Experimental Section.

unit_operations.name: Solution Preparation
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: polyacrylonitrile (PAN) and Ru3+/Fe3+ metal salts were uniformly mixed in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF)

nodes.source_text: The preparation process of Ru-Fe7C3@CNF via the electrospinning method is illustrated in the Scheme 1. First, the polyacrylonitrile (PAN) and Ru3+/Fe3+ metal salts were uniformly mixed in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF). As follows, the Ru-Fe7C3@CNF catalyst was obtained by electrospinning, pre-oxidation, and annealing steps. The detailed synthesis method is in the Experimental Section.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1.0 M KOH three-electrode setup
nodes.source_text: Ru-Fe₇C₃@CNF exhibits enhanced HER activity based on the linear voltammetric curves (LSV) analysis. It only requires overpotentials of 29 and 116 mV to reach a current density of 10 and 100 mA cm⁻², respectively, which is significantly lower than that of 20% Pt/C (35, 225 mV), Ru@CNF (72, 212 mV), and Fe₇C₃@CNF (200, 452 mV), even the overpotential of 232 mV to achieve the large current density of 0.5 A cm⁻²... The Ru-Fe₇C₃@CNF shows the high mass activity of 1.17 A mg⁻¹_Ru at overpotential 100 mV... the lowest Tafel slope of 21.5 mV dec⁻¹... Ru-Fe₇C₃@CNF possesses the lowest charge transfer resistance (R_ct)
The durability measures of Ru-Fe₇C₃@CNF catalysts were performed at the current density of 20 mA cm⁻² with continuous catalysis for 100 h... which shows no significant reduction in current density.

nodes.description: AEMWE performance with NiFe LDH anode at 80°C
nodes.source_text: the assembled anion exchange membrane water electrolysis device utilizing Ru-Fe₇C₃@CNF//NiFe LDH operates at a voltage of 1.67 and 1.81 V at the current density of 0.5 and 1 A cm⁻², respectively, and... show high stability for 300 h under 0.5 A cm⁻² in alkaline medium.

nodes.characterization_summary: Two-phase structure consists of Ru and Fe7C3, evidenced by peaks corresponding to Ru (JCPDS: 06-0663) and Fe7C3 (JCPDS: 17-0333).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) reveals that the two-phase structure consists of Ru and Fe7C3, as evidenced by the peaks corresponding to the standard PDF cards of Ru (JCPDS: 06-0663) and Fe7C3 (JCPDS: 17-0333) in Figure S1a-c.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-Fe7C3@CNF presents a 1D cross-linked nanofiber network structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images show that Ru-Fe7C3@CNF presents a 1D cross-linked nanofiber network structure, favoring electron transmission in Figure S1d.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nanoparticles embedded in CNFs with diameter of 150 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 1a, the TEM images illustrate that the nanoparticles are embedded in CNFs with a diameter of 150 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice spacing of 2.01 Å and 2.16 Å corresponds to (211) plane of Fe7C3 and (002) plane of Ru, respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To determine the phase structure of the nanoparticles, the high-resolution TEM image in Figure 1b also confirms that the lattice spacing of 2.01 and 2.16 Å corresponds to the (211) plane of the Fe7C3 and (002) plane of the Ru, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction rings confirm presence of mixed phases of Ru and Fe7C3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, the corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) with diffraction rings of the crystal plane confirms the presence of mixed phases of Ru and Fe7C3 in Figure 1c.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-Fe7C3 nanoparticles with diameter of 30 nm embedded in CNFs; lattice spacing of 2.27 Å and 2.34 Å corresponds to (002) plane of Fe7C3 and (100) plane of Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The low-magnification HAADF-STEM in Figure 1d reveals that a significant number of bright-colored Ru-Fe7C3 nanoparticles with a diameter of 30 nm are embedded in CNFs, and high-resolution HAADF-STEM images also illustrate that a hetero-interface between two kinds of lattices (Figures 1d and S2 and S3), where the lattice spacing of 2.27 and 2.34 Å corresponds to the (002) plane of the Fe7C3 and (100) plane of the Ru, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe L-edge characteristic peak (710 eV) exhibits significant energy negative shift across the interfacial region.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EELS line scan analysis performed along the direction of the yellow arrow shown in Figure 1e showed that the Fe L-edge characteristic peak (710 eV) exhibited a significant energy negative shift phenomenon across the interfacial region.

nodes.characterization_summary: Significant lattice stress present at twin boundary defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, significant lattice stress is present at the defects based on the geometric phase analysis (GPA) in Figure 1g.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniformly dispersed C, Fe, and Ru elements in nanoparticles loaded into CNFs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As demonstrated in Figures 1h and S4, elemental distribution results confirm that the nanoparticles with uniformly dispersed C, Fe, and Ru elements are loaded into the CNFs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Atom ratio of Fe and Ru is 1.3:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) measurements validate that the atom ratio of Fe and Ru is 1.3:1 in Table S1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elements Ru, Fe, C present; C 1s shows M-C and C-C peaks indicating Fe-C bonds and graphitized carbon skeletons; Fe electron-deficient consistent with EELS; Ru valence state (0.044) lower than Ru@CNF (0.071).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) spectrum shows that the elements of Ru, Fe, and C exist in Figure S5a. The C 1s spectrum presents characteristic peaks of M–C and C–C... The phenomenon is consistent with the EELS and XPS analyses in Figures 1e and S5c... consistent with the XPS analysis results in Figure S5d.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe K-edge absorption edge higher than Fe7C3@CNF indicating electron-deficient Fe; Ru K-edge lower than Ru@CNF located between Ru foil and RuO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe K-edge absorption edge of Ru-Fe7C3@CNF is higher than that of Fe7C3@CNF in Figure 2a... The Ru K-edge absorption edge of Ru-Fe7C3@CNF is lower than that of Ru@CNF and is located between the Ru foil and RuO2 in Figure 2d.
